props.title: NarmadaQA: A Two-Hop Question Answering Dataset over Encyclopedic Text
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering
DenseHop: Iterative Dense Retrieval for Multi-Hop Questions
props.abstract: Multi-hop questions require evidence from several passages, and a single retrieval step often misses the second passage. We present DenseHop, an iterative dense retriever that reformulates the query after each hop using the passages retrieved so far. On the two-hop NarmadaQA benchmark, DenseHop reaches 61.3 exact match (EM), compared with 54.8 EM for the sparse ChainTFIDF retriever. Iterative dense retrieval outperforms sparse chain retrieval on two-hop questions. We release code and trained encoders.

props.title: KaveriHop: A Benchmark for Two- and Three-Hop Question Answering
props.abstract: Existing multi-hop QA benchmarks mostly contain two-hop questions. We introduce KaveriHop, a benchmark of 18,400 English questions split into 2-hop and 3-hop subsets, each with annotated bridge entities and supporting passages. Baselines degrade sharply with more hops: DenseHop falls from 48.2 EM on 2-hop to 31.5 EM on 3-hop questions. We release the data, the bridge-entity annotations and an evaluation script.

props.title: GraphWalker-QA: Answering Multi-Hop Questions by Walking Entity Graphs
props.abstract: We propose GraphWalker-QA, which builds an entity graph over the corpus and answers multi-hop questions by walking from question entities to answer passages. On KaveriHop, GraphWalker-QA improves over DenseHop by 2.1 EM on 2-hop and 7.9 EM on 3-hop questions. Walking an entity graph gives larger gains on 3-hop questions than on 2-hop questions, suggesting that explicit structure helps longer reasoning chains.

props.title: HopRank: Hop-Aware Reranking for Dense Multi-Hop Retrieval
props.abstract: We present HopRank, which extends DenseHop with a hop-aware reranker that re-scores candidate passage chains using cross-attention between hops. On KaveriHop, HopRank reaches 53.4 EM on 2-hop and 36.0 EM on 3-hop questions, adding only 30 ms of latency per query. Hop-aware reranking closes the gap to graph-based retrieval on 2-hop questions but not on 3-hop questions.

props.title: TriHop-Bench: Stress-Testing Retrieval on Three- and Four-Hop Questions
props.abstract: We introduce TriHop-Bench, 6,000 English questions requiring three or four reasoning hops, and evaluate three published retrievers using their released code. All of them lose accuracy as hops increase, but the graph-based GW-QA degrades least. The advantage of graph-based retrieval over dense retrieval grows as the number of hops increases.

props.title: GraphFuse: Fusing Dense and Graph Retrieval for Multi-Hop QA
props.abstract: Dense and graph-based retrievers fail on different questions. GraphFuse runs a GraphWalker-QA walk and a HopRank chain search in parallel and merges their candidate chains with a learned fusion scorer. GraphFuse reaches 57.9 and 46.3 EM on KaveriHop 2-hop and 3-hop, and 41.2 and 22.7 EM on TriHop-Bench 3-hop and 4-hop. Fusing dense and graph retrieval outperforms either approach alone at every hop count.

props.title: VaigaiQA: Multi-Hop Question Answering in Tamil
props.abstract: We introduce VaigaiQA, 5,200 two-hop questions written natively in Tamil over Tamil encyclopedic text. We evaluate Dense-Hop and GraphWalker-QA, using the LinkLite entity linker to build the graph. Unlike results reported for English, the graph-based method trails the dense one: 30.2 versus 33.0 EM. LinkLite links only 61.0% of Tamil mentions correctly. On Tamil questions, graph-based retrieval performs worse than dense retrieval because entity linking is unreliable.

props.title: Revisiting Graph Gains: A Reproduction Study of GraphWalker-QA
props.abstract: We reproduce GraphWalker-QA on KaveriHop. With the gold entity annotations used in the original paper we match its results (39.5 versus 39.8 EM on 3-hop questions). With entity links predicted by LinkLite, 3-hop EM drops to 35.1, slightly below HopRank at 35.4. GraphWalker-QA's 3-hop advantage depends on gold entity links; with predicted links it falls below HopRank.

props.title: Erratum: GraphFuse: Fusing Dense and Graph Retrieval for Multi-Hop QA
props.abstract: A bug in our evaluation script counted some 4-hop answers with trailing punctuation as correct. The corrected 4-hop exact match of GraphFuse on TriHop-Bench is 19.4, not 22.7 as published. All other numbers are unchanged.

props.title: LiteGraphFuse: Distilling Fused Retrieval for Small Language Models
props.abstract: GraphFuse is accurate but slow, which limits its use with small language models and on modest hardware. LiteGraphFuse distils the GraphFuse fusion scorer into a 3-billion-parameter student and prunes the graph walk to two expansions per hop. On KaveriHop it reaches 55.0 and 43.9 EM, 95% of GraphFuse, at 105 ms per query instead of 420 ms. On the Tamil VaigaiQA benchmark it reaches 38.6 EM, above both Dense-Hop and GraphWalker-QA.

props.title: Entity Linking Is the Bottleneck: Error Analysis of Graph Retrieval in Low-Resource Languages
props.abstract: Two recent findings question graph-based multi-hop retrieval: a reproduction study found that GraphWalker-QA's 3-hop gains need gold entity links, and a Tamil benchmark found graph retrieval below dense retrieval. We analyse 600 failed questions from both settings. In 71% of failures the first wrong step is an entity-linking error. LinkLite reaches 84.0% accuracy on English KaveriHop passages but 61.0% on Tamil. Low entity-linking accuracy explains both the failed reproduction of GraphWalker-QA and the drop of graph retrieval on Tamil.

props.title: HopLens: Interpretable Path Scoring for Multi-Hop Retrieval
props.abstract: Multi-hop retrievers rarely explain why a chain of passages was chosen. HopLens scores each candidate chain with an interpretable path-aware reranking module that assigns a weight to every hop transition. HopLens reaches 56.2 and 44.8 EM on KaveriHop 2-hop and 3-hop, and 39.5 EM on TriHop-Bench 3-hop. HopLens achieves state-of-the-art exact match on 3-hop questions in both KaveriHop and TriHop-Bench.
